An estimation of the $B^0_s\rightarrow K^+K^-$ decay time for $B^0_s$ mesons has been made with the help of around 37 picobarns of LHCb data from 2010. This measure allows for constraints on theories beyond the Standard Model that may influence the $B^0_s$ system and was found to be 1.440 picoseconds by employing two methods with varying degrees of uncertainty, specifically 0.096 (statistical) ± 0.008 (systematic) ± 0.003 (model-based).

This research paper focuses on the numerical solution of a stochastic control problem governed by a parabolic equation with the control variable affecting the diffusion coefficient, particularly with the presence of rough inputs; it establishes the convergence of a specific numerical discretization method and provides an alternative solution using a stochastic simulation technique known as the Monte-Carlo method.

Our in-depth examination of extremely energetic cosmic rays detected at the Pierre Auger Observatory reveals significant patterns of large-scale anisotropy. At the higher end of our energy range, a specific anisotropy signal was initially reported - namely, a right ascension-based dipolar modulation. To further investigate, we divided the most energetic group into three segments, and discovered that this anisotropy becomes increasingly pronounced with rising energy levels above 4 EeV, exhibiting an energy-dependent pattern that adheres to a power law with an index of 0.79 ± 0.19. We also discovered that the orientation of these anisotropy patterns supports their extragalactic origins, across all energy levels examined. Furthermore, an investigation of quadrupolar components revealed no substantial variation in preferred directions or angular distribution, resulting in an empty rate that is consistent with expectations and has an angular distribution parameter of λ1 = -0.026 ± 0.015.

The ATLAS detector at the LHC gathered p+Pb data with a centre of mass energy of 5.02 TeV and 25 nanobarns of integrated luminosity, enabling a comparison with interpolated pp measurements at 2.76 and 7 TeV. Owing to its sophisticated design and reliability, the ATLAS detector successfully collected a comprehensive dataset during heavy ion and proton-proton runs. As a result, it facilitated precise measurements of the nuclear modification factor, obtained by dividing charged particle yields from heavy ion collisions by their proton-proton counterparts in various centrality ranges and rapidity intervals. Furthermore, this analysis reveals a notable variation in the nuclear modification factor with transverse momentum, showing a more pronounced trend in more peripheral collisions.

Quantum mechanics can be explored on noncommutative spaces, characterized by specific commutation relations that define the structure constants of a Lie algebra. By transforming the coordinates into linear differential operators in a commuting momentum space, we can reformulate this issue into an ordinary quantum problem. These operators, representing the coordinates $\hat x_a$, have a form $-i\hat D_a = -iE_{ab}(p)\partial /\partial p_b$, where $E_{ab}$ can be expressed as an infinite series over the deformation parameter $\theta$. The deformed Hamiltonian $\hat H$ describes the motion on corresponding group manifolds with sizes proportional to $\theta^{-1}$, whose metrics also appear in certain infinite series of $\theta$. The matrices $E_{ab}$ can be represented in simple forms for certain algebras like $su(2)$ and $u(N)$, allowing us to extract associated Hamiltonians and retrieve their spectral properties. Notably, this approach yields new, irreducible noncommutative Hamiltonians with classical counterparts on Lie group manifolds.

In evaluating the potential of federated learning, we tested its performance in training deep learning models to analyze digitized tissue samples, specifically in a classification application involving the detection of tumor cells within whole-slide images. By simulating a FL environment with a large, diverse dataset of cancer images from various sources, we compared the results of training models using both a federated approach and a centralized approach. Our findings indicate that federated learning can produce models with similar accuracy to those trained with centralized data, while avoiding the need to collect extensive training datasets at a single location. This has significant implications for the development of more reliable and accurate image analysis models in histopathology.

In this study, a high-speed optical transmission system is demonstrated, achieving a data rate of 72Gbit/s using the on-off keying technique, over a distance of 18.8km in a South China Sea submarine cable that lacks dispersion compensation. The experimental results show that random laser sources can be utilized in optical transmission systems to compensate for the effects of chromatic dispersion.

Deep Learning models like Temporal Convolutional Networks (TCNs) hold great promise for handling time-series data. TCNs leverage a technique called time-dilated convolution that poses an optimization challenge which typically demands significant experimentation. We've developed a technique to automate the dilation optimization process by casting it as a weight-pruning operation along the time axis. Our method learns dilation factors concurrently with weights during training and achieves notable gains in model compactness and inference efficiency without compromising accuracy. It produces a range of highly optimal TCN variants from a single starting model, surpassing the performance of custom-designed networks in both efficiency and accuracy.
This paper proves that any finite-dimensional Zinbiel algebra over a given field possesses a specific characteristic - nilpotency, building on a previous discovery that these algebras are solvable.

This study provides first-time data on the fluctuations of a specific angle, known as $\Psi_n$, and magnitude, known as $v_n$, related to particle flow, which have been determined using a newly developed technique for four-particle correlations. Researchers used ALICE to collect these data in high-energy Pb-Pb collisions at the LHC. Fluctuations in both angle and magnitude are evident across different centralities and become more pronounced in more central collisions and in collisions where the momentum of the particles is higher than 2 GeV/c. These findings, which have been compared to theoretical models such as iEBE-VISHNU, MUSIC, and AMPT, shed new light on the complex and not well understood initial conditions of these collisions. Furthermore, they highlight unique sensitivities to two crucial factors: the viscosity of quark--gluon plasma and the characteristics of the collisions' initial state. Given that these fluctuations tend to increase with the momentum of the particles, there is a need for re-examining existing theoretical models to gain a more precise and unbiased understanding of quark--gluon plasma's properties.

The unified correspondence theory leverages the algebraic and order theoretic underpinnings of Sahlqvist correspondence to offer versatile tools for correspondence and canonicity across diverse semantic frameworks and signatures. These tools, specifically tailored to logics whose semantics rely on normal lattice expansions (DLEs), enable computation of first-order correspondents for inductive formulas using the algorithm ALBA. Conversely, the standard algebraic semantics for classical first-order logic fails to capture the inductive formula's correspondent accurately due to defects in its algebraic representation, a phenomenon known as the "double negation shift." To rectify this, an alternative algebraic semantics is proposed, reflecting the inductive formula's first-order correspondent through the ALBA algorithm's adaptation to the proposed semantics, resulting in the respondent's constructibility via the ALBA algorithm in the proposed semantics.

This research focuses on addressing inconsistencies in data tables that contain missing values and functional relationships. Unlike conventional approaches that require adherence to these dependencies, this work aims to explore and resolve instances that breach them. We view inconsistencies as an integral aspect of our problem, seeking to represent problems with partial and redundant data while observing specified theories that may also be incomplete or containing exceptions. We view a plausible interpretation as a logical framework, utilizing first-order classical predicates and exceptions to model functional dependencies. We view the problem as determining whether a given set of facts can result in a specific instance of a relation, rather than checking if a universal statement holds. We examine how minimal solutions (those with fewest additional values) relate to retrenchment, in order to avoid unnecessarily increasing data. We also explore the connection between this problem and non-monotonic reasoning, particularly the exception handling in the Gelfond-Lifschitz approach. We operate with an open world assumption, where we can incorporate external values into our table to resolve redundancies. We establish that our problem is computationally more demanding, falling in the category of the hardest complete sets of classical axioms in the language with strong negation, in contrast to the commonly accepted equivalence between logic programs with exceptions and circumscription under the closed world assumption.

This study presents a novel dynamic econometric model called Time-Varying Poisson AutoRegressive with external covariates, specifically designed to analyze and forecast count-based time series data. Our research indicates that a score-driven approach is particularly effective in capturing the evolution of time-varying parameters and allows for modeling complex dynamics and shifts within such data sets. Furthermore, we have analyzed the theoretical characteristics of the TV-PARX model, demonstrating under mild conditions that maximum likelihood estimation yields reliable and normally-distributed estimates of model parameters. To evaluate the TV-PARX model's performance and forecasting capabilities in real-world scenarios, we conducted a series of Monte Carlo simulations. Additionally, we have applied the time-varying specification of the TV-PARX model to empirical data sets, analyzing new daily COVID-19 cases in Italy and corporate defaults in the US.

We introduce Neural Descriptor Fields (NDFs), a novel object representation that
replicates both object points and relative poses in relation to a target, using
category-level descriptors. We apply this representation in object manipulation,
with the aim of repeating tasks on new object instances from the same category
after witnessing a single demonstration. To achieve this, we use optimization
to locate the pose whose descriptor corresponds to that in the demonstration. NDFs
are efficiently trained without expert input, using a self-supervised 3D
auto-encoder, and exhibit robust performance across 6-DoF rotations and translations.
In experiments, NDFs master tasks from just a handful of 3D demonstrations (captured
from a camera looking down the z-axis) and successfully execute tasks on both
individual trials and under varying time and motion conditions with zero
additional training. Notably, NDFs are the first optimization-based object
representation to perform tasks correctly on new instances of the same object
category. As a bonus, NDFs outperform previous methods in aligned pose detection,
matching their performance while surpassing it in unaligned cases.

The SiD Detector is one of the two validated detector designs for the future ILC, specifically tailored to meet precision demands for the Higgs boson and other research areas while maintaining an adaptable sensitivity to diverse potential discoveries. The SiD's robust silicon vertex and tracking system, complemented by its high central magnetic field, ensures precise momentum measurement. The detector's finely granulated calorimeter system, designed for particle flow analysis, delivers accurate energy resolution across a wide energy range. Given the approaching construction timeline for the ILC, the time has come to reassess the design choices made during the design phase and incorporate the recent breakthroughs in technology into the review process. This review will discuss R&D prospects and participation opportunities for the SiD's development areas.

We performed the first in-depth analysis of seven red giant members in the globular cluster Tononzintla 2. We used the APOGEE-2 near-infrared spectra to examine the abundance levels of multiple chemical species in these stars. The findings showed a moderate metal content and the absence of an internal variation in metal abundance. Tononzintla 2 displayed an increased presence of alpha-enrichment which aligns with patterns observed in other rich-metallic galactic clusters. A nitrogen spread was discovered in Tononzintla 2 with multiple nitrogen-rich stars residing within it, significantly above average levels for this region, suggesting a multi-generational population within the cluster that consists of first-generation nitrogen-abundance members. A carbon spread, however, was not evident within the cluster as its magnitude fell below the measurement uncertainty. A radial velocity mean for Tonzontla 2 was determined to be -128.4 $km/s$ and an associated velocity dispersion of 2.7 $km/s$. When compared to APOGEE-2 spectra for the A0III star Vega, the galaxy systematics were found to introduce minimal bias in abundance measurements, suggesting that the observed patterns are genuine and not the result of observational artifacts.

The Isabelle Archive of Formal Proofs has amassed substantial size over recent years, representing an impressive compilation of research and offering a diverse range of opportunities for statistical exploration in the field of theorem proving. Despite the numerous contributions made so far, the ever-expanding nature of the archive still poses certain challenges: locating specific content has become increasingly difficult, making it essential to prioritize reuse and clarity of comprehension. This thesis proposal outlines my research objectives, which focus on these concerns, as well as initial findings, which reveal that the Isabelle Archive exhibits characteristics typical of scale-free networks, as evidenced by the distribution of node in-degrees in its dependency graph.

Using the functional renormalization group at the next-to-leading order in the derivative expansion, we have updated the position of the Yang-Lee edge singularity for O(N) universality classes in classic scenarios. Specifically for QCD's relevant universality classes in three dimensions, we have determined $|z_c|/R_\chi^{1/\gamma}$ to be approximately 1.607, 1.589, and 1.58 for 'x' of 0.255, 0.08, and 0 respectively. Furthermore, we have found similar values for $|z_c|/R_\chi^{1/\gamma}$ in three-dimensional O(N) universality classes to be 1.602, 1.589, and 1.58 respectively. These findings are derived from an epsilon expansion that has been evaluated to two-loop and three-loop orders.

In statistics and machine learning, it is frequently essential to establish whether a basic optimization method on a non-convex function can eventually enter a region where the function becomes locally convex. To address this, we developed an inequality that enables us to analyze the properties of the optimization landscape surrounding the solutions produced by an approximate message passing (AMP) algorithm. Specifically, we applied our inequality to demonstrate the local convexity of a particular TAP free energy function, which is relevant to the Z2 synchronization problem and the Sherrington-Kirkpatrick model. Additionally, our inequality led to a confirmation of a previous conjecture regarding the efficiency of a sampling algorithm in the "easy" regime of these models.

Modern metasurfaces, at the intersection of advanced technology and science,  
constitute an intricate field, involving electromagnetic systems characterized by  
thin, expansive, and minutely featured particles that can also vary spatially,  
temporally, and linearly.  To tackle this intricacy, researchers need to employ a  
unified approach that integrates appropriate modeling methods, design principles,  
measurement techniques, theoretical constraints, and engineering applications.  
This paper begins with an in-depth examination of what defines a metasurface,  
followed by a discussion on parameterization methods for these structures,  
then explores their use in manipulating light and other wave systems, as well as  
the development of negative and high-impedance transmission line structures,  
and finally touches on control applications, including linear and non-linear  
systems.  This comprehensive analysis is complemented by essential measurement  
protocols, mathematical limitations of metasurfaces, and a range of  
applications spanning wireless technology, optical systems, and acoustic  
engineering.

The primary objective of this research is to validate the smooth local orbital linearization theorem for smooth vector fields with a full set of nearby first integrals, especially those at nondegenerate singular points. This theoretical validation relies heavily on key concepts, including the formal orbital linearization theorem for formally integrable vector fields, the application of the blowing-up technique, and the application of the Sternberg-Chen theorem regarding formally equivalent smooth hyperbolic vector fields.

This report outlines a deep learning approach known as the Electron Correlation
Potential Neural Network (eCPNN), which can learn simplified potential functions
that accurately capture the intricate instantaneous relationships among electrons
within complex atomic systems. Trained in an unsupervised manner with constrained
data derived from Full Configuration Interaction one-electron density functions, the
eCPNN model effectively predicts total atomic energies with remarkable precision.

We have serendipitously identified a massive arc-like structure, dubbed a Giant Arc, which lies at a redshift of approximately 0.8. Spanning nearly 1 billion light-years, this feature exhibits remarkable symmetry when viewed from space. It was discovered through a novel approach using intervening magnesium-absorbing systems in the light from background quasars. Our analysis leverages a range of techniques, including statistical tests, theoretical calculations, and visual inspections to confirm the presence and one-dimensional extent of the arc. We also explore whether similar structures could form a significant part of the universe's large-scale structure, but this is limited by present understanding of their three-dimensional form. Furthermore, we have uncovered other dLIM arcs at similar distances, which together suggest a possible distribution of the arc lengths. This finding holds potential for expanding our comprehension of the universe's structure on a massive scale and may influence future missions like CRAFT and DESI.

While using photometry from stars to monitor the atmosphere may seem uncomplicated for optical astrophysics, achieving a precision of 0.01 for measuring the aerosol depth has been challenging. By taking wide-field photometry over a broad altitude range, the aerosol depth can be determined quickly, regardless of the system's absolute calibration, and even provides calibration as a by-product. Our team used extensive data from the FRAM telescope at the Pierre Auger Observatory and a similar telescope at the Cherenkov Telescope Array site to improve the precision of this technique to a precision of possibly 0.01. To accomplish this, we conducted precise laboratory measurements of the system's response to varying light intensities and spectra to counter the limitations of non-linear CCD detectors under observation conditions.

Recently, estimating a 6D object pose using Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) has gained significant interest. Literature can be broadly categorized into two main areas based on whether intermediate cues are employed: direct methods and two-stage pipelines. In the latter category, CNN regresses intermediate cues such as object coordinates or virtual control points instead of pose parameters in the initial stage. Object pose is then resolved through the construction of correspondence points utilizing reasoning capabilities of traditional PnP algorithms. This survey delves into the two stategies of two-stage pipelines, comprehensively reviewing state-of-the-art models that have emerged over the past five years. We also summarize key performance metrics and datasets utilized by these two stages, as well as discuss future research directions in this domain.

Peridynamic theories have seen a significant expansion in their application across multiple disciplines, due to their ability to model and track discontinuity formation within materials. Bond-based Peridynamics, despite its modeling restrictions, has become a widely-used approach in numerical simulations because of its ease of implementation and intuitive connection to real-world physics. This paper delves into the aspects of bond-based peridynamic models, providing a thorough examination of the theory and its numerical representations. Various bond-based PD integral kernels have been presented along with their distinguishing characteristics, leading to discussions on their implications and common traits. A closer examination was conducted on the role of non-locality in determining motion, the interplay between kernel structure and material non-penetration, as well as the influence of PD kernel non-linearity on predicting fracture development. Finally, an exploration was initiated on adapting BB-PD to model fluids within the context of fading memory materials, suggesting directions for enhanced understanding of fluid dynamics through peridynamics.

We present GGLasso, a Python library designed to address General Graphical Lasso
challenges. Based on the original work of Friedman (2007), Graphical Lasso
estimates a sparsely constructed inverse covariance matrix $\Theta$ from
multivariate Gaussian data $\mathcal{X}$, initially introduced by Dempster (1972)
under Covariance Selection. The framework has been expanded to accommodate
hidden variables in Chandrasekaran (2012) and can jointly estimate multiple
inverse covariance matrices, as shown in Danaher (2013) and Tomasi (2018). The
GGLasso package supports the resolution of diverse formulations and notable
subcases like Graphical Lasso with latent variables, Group, and Fused Graphical Lasso.

Numerous numerical methods for resolving stochastic differential equations in molecular dynamics simulations have been scrutinized and assessed, focusing on deterministic impulses, drifts, Brownian motions, and molecular environments. Building on previous work, this study extends the comparison of these methods within the context of biomolecular simulations, utilizing two models and evaluating the accuracy of configurational averaging over time. The results indicate that methods determined by the way they discretize the Brownian motion can yield highly precise outcomes in terms of physical consistency and configurational accuracy, even in biomolecular simulations that incorporate strong fluctuating forces. In fact, these methods can accurately reproduce experimental and other theoretical findings in solvated biomolecular simulations using the harmonic oscillator model, and they outperform commonly used algorithms in calculating the probability distribution of biomolecular helix lengths. Furthermore, the proposed molecule-solvent approach demonstrates the superiority of certain integration schemes, such as the BAOAB algorithm, in calculating biomolecular extension probabilities under varying solvent conditions. The findings suggest that advanced integration methods can efficiently and accurately simulate biopolymers in solution, providing a foundation for incorporating these algorithms into rigorous equilibrium and kinetic biomolecular simulations.

Numerical relativity simulations allow us to study how binary black hole mergers interact with their surroundings. However, these simulations start only shortly before the merger and require predetermined initial conditions to proceed. Therefore, a significant task involves identifying the appropriate configuration for the binary system and its environment at this point in the process. In this research, we investigate the behavior of dark matter concentrated in a dense core within a galactic bulge as it orbits a binary system, specifically looking at a dwarf galaxy where this phenomenon may be observable using upcoming galaxy mergers detected with JWST and the LSST. We develop a straightforward mathematical framework to model the distribution of this dark matter, then employ a two-dimensional relativistic hydrodynamics/matter flow simulation to test our assumptions and examine the properties of the system at the start of the merger. Our findings show that for binaries with significant mass, the dark matter core merges directly with the black holes, whereas for smaller mass binaries, there is a distinct peak in density forming at the Lagrange point $L_1$, where the binary system ejections create a rarefied region. These findings have implications for detecting gravitational waves generated by matter falling into the binary or ripples in spacetime caused by disturbances in the dark matter, and they highlight the importance of further observational studies, specifically looking for systems with a visible galaxy and no active nucleus to find the kind of dwarf galaxies where this phenomenon may occur.

We tackle the persistent issue of exponential stability for a stretched Euler-Bernoulli beam on a star-shaped graph with three equal branches. The outer points where these branches meet are fixed while rotating. The inner point is capable of moving in two ways, with rotational movement influenced by damping. A detailed analysis in a Hilbert space reveals how the spectrum's asymptotic distribution and structure evolve. It demonstrates that specific eigenvector characteristics form a complete and orthonormal basis, which directly impacts the condition for exponential stability. Notably, we show that under certain shape conditions of the graph, the spectrum behaves in a predictable manner with an infinite, discrete distribution and specific density properties.

Researchers utilized acoustic lenses composed of PMMA to increase the detection area of sensitive devices and improve resolution. Although effective, PMMA lens lens lenses exhibited significant distortion due to their curvature. To overcome this limitation and maintain improved detection advantages, a new ultrasound filling material must possess specific properties including high acoustic impedance, low attenuation, and low elasticity. After evaluating multiple materials including PMMA, PEBAX, and Stycast 1090SI, it was determined that Stycast 1090SI offered the best combination of properties. This research demonstrated that adding a Stycast 1090SI lens increased the detection area and resolution of sensitive devices, allowing for more compact and efficient designs. The new design allowed for more flat detection areas, improved depth estimation, and better size estimation, leading to better overall performance. Further research is required to optimize the lens properties and apply this concept to other materials including flexible lenses.

Our new method calculates a variation of eigenvector centrality for multi-layered networks that incorporate node importance across different layers. In these networks, defined by separate interconnected graphs without connections between different layers, the value of a node's centrality is determined by the sum of the values of the connected nodes within each specific layer, similar to traditional eigenvector centrality calculations. Unlike standard approaches, our approach takes into account the relationships between different network layers and their respective impact on the centrality values. Unlike current multi-layer eigenvector centrality frameworks that account for inter-layer connections, our approach uses a separate set of equations that can be solved using a hybrid algorithm.

We tackle the issue of non-blind deblurring and demosaicking on noisy raw images using a learning-based approach tailored to handle these images directly, with an innovative new component that simultaneously demosaicks and deblurs them in an interpretable way. To train this model, we utilize real-world camera data transformed into raw images through a realistic process, mimicking real-world camera functions. By doing so, we demonstrate the advantages of our single-stage model over traditional approaches combining demosaicking and deblurring modules, according to objective performance metrics. Additionally, our model has the capacity to remove a camera's inherent blurring effect, enabling successful demosaicking of images that appear blurred in raw form. To verify the reliability of this assumption, we develop a novel metric for quantitatively assessing demosaicking performance on non-blurred images with varying levels of blur. Our model also exhibits promising results in removing the inherent blurring effect of camera sensors, with successful examples of demosaicking images with varying levels of inherent blur.

Recently, we generated the $R$-Poincar\'e algebra using deformed Poisson brackets, 
which effectively replicate the Fock coordinate transformation. This transformation 
corresponds to a de Sitter spacetime. In this study, we formulate the Dirac equation within 
$R$-Minkowski spacetime and establish that it is analogous to the Dirac equation defined 
within the de Sitter spacetime, described by its conformally flat metric. We then propose 
a novel strategy to solve the Dirac equation within the de Sitter spacetime by adopting 
the Schr\"{o}dinger picture.

This study introduces an open source Python framework that utilizes background knowledge and observational data for the purpose of inferring causal relationships. This framework is comprised of the 'cdt' package, which executes a comprehensive causal discovery process to identify the causal interactions and the causal network structure among the variables, drawing from established methodologies including those from 'Bnlearn' and 'Pcalg', in addition to pairwise algorithms like ANM. The framework is available on GitHub under the terms of the permissive MIT License.

This study investigates how spheres interact with water upon impact, specifically the process known as surface seal that occurs as the sphere enters the water's surface. This surface seal regime, found between low and high-speed impact velocities, features a distinctive "splash dome" formation. Empirical rules describing when the splash dome closes ("pinch-off time") generally hold for both slow-moving and fast-moving spheres, yet require further refinement, especially in the middle speed range. In fact, at mid-range speeds, pinch-off times relate differently to fluid dynamics than they do at either low or high speeds, indicating that existing models need modification. In this work, pinch-off times are re-expressed in terms of a parameter combining both fluid and solid components, and a single continuity equation is established to represent all impact speeds.

A well-known hypothesis posits that gravity at a quantum level must be devoid of universal symmetries. We studied an array of Type IIB four-dimensional $\mathcal{N}=2$ effective field theories to uncover the range of universal symmetries potentially present and then investigated why they are avoided. Generalized $\theta$-terms emerge as crucial elements in these theories. These $\theta$-terms generate non-linear connections between axion fields and gravitational components, as well as universal sectors. However, the string theory framework for string compactifications implies that these terms can be arbitrarily scaled. Consequently, any form of universal symmetry within these calculations is intrinsically fragile and can be broken upon minor modifications to the compactification parameters.

Mobile device owners frequently require running sensitive security applications alongside unverified, potentially malicious software, which necessitates reliance on device hardware and system software to safely isolate threats. 

This often misplaced trust is the foundation on which our objective is built – namely to minimize the reliance on device hardware and software components for users to withstand cyber threats. 

We introduce an innovative multi-domain hardware setup consisting of isolated sections, where programs are partitioned statically to prevent malicious interaction. 

A few key hardware components with proven security functionality are integrated to grant secure temporary access to processing resources and external input/output interfaces simultaneously.

To manage these hardware components, we introduce OctopOS, a unique OS comprising several secure subsystems working together in distrust. 

We showcase a functioning prototype, incorporating our hardware and software, utilizing a combined CPU-FPGA board with an acceptable additional hardware expense in comparison to existing SoCs. 

We observe substantial reductions in trust requirements for security applications using our device, delivering better security performance compared to standard security frameworks, with little performance impact for non-security programs, matching the speed of traditional systems.

We investigated the challenges of robust reinforcement learning in scenarios where an adaptive adversary intentionally manipulates rewards and transition probabilities. The adversary's influence is confined to no more than an $\epsilon$ fraction of all training episodes. Notably, this attack model surpasses previously considered methods. We established a key finding that no reinforcement learning algorithm can discover an optimal policy better than $O(\epsilon)$ under these circumstances. Interestingly, we discovered that the natural policy gradient method can be robust when the corruption is bounded and is capable of finding an $O(\sqrt{\epsilon})$-optimal policy. We developed a Filtered Policy Gradient (FPG) algorithm, capable of tolerating unbounded reward corruption, and achieved an $O(\epsilon^{1/4})$-optimal policy. The FPG algorithm represents a pioneering solution to robust reinforcement learning in scenarios with significant adversarial interference. Moreover, we verified the effectiveness of an FPG implementation utilizing a neural network on MuJoCo continuous control benchmarks.

We uncover an unselectable version of the box game paradox, featuring players making remarkably accurate predictions of unknown real numbers without access to relevant information. Additionally, our analysis confirms the requirement of choice in solving the classic problem and examines alternative configurations of the game.

Our calculations using first-principles methods reveal that cubanite exhibits unusual orbital selectivity, with electrons occupying certain molecular orbitals while being localized in other atomic ones. This phenomenon is exceptionally rare in 3d transition metal compounds, providing a theoretical basis for the experimentally observed lack of charge disproportionation, anomalous Mössbauer spectra, and ferromagnetic coupling between adjacent iron ions.

A burgeoning field in quantum physics, known as multi-phonon physics, is driving research and development for both fundamental understanding and applications in metrology and communication systems. Quantum acoustic resonators serve as the ideal testing ground for multi-phonon phenomena through a combination of theoretical and experimental studies. Theoretical models and simulations are combined with experimental data to study the characteristics of "dark" and "bright" excitons, interacting with multiple acoustic phonons within semiconductor quantum dots. It has been found that "dark" excitons, which have a higher stability and longevity than "bright" excitons, can achieve bright lasing with a high spin purity when emitting a single photon. The inelastic scattering between a "dark" exciton and a "bright" exciton can result in the emission of a phonon pair, while a "bright" exciton can be scattered into "dark" states by absorbing a phonon. A key breakthrough has been the observation of bright and dark excitons in resonance with a phonon, known as bright-dark exciton doublet (BDD), which has a dark state component and can be converted from a bright state component by a phonon. The BDD can be used to study the characteristics of a quantum acoustic resonator, such as its stiffness and mass, and understand the formation of a phonon. The BDD can also be used to investigate the interaction between a quantum dot and a quantum acoustic resonator, and understand the multi-phonon

Our investigation focuses on a 2D electronic lattice from a non-symmorphic wallpaper group.  We're examining a herringbone lattice with two types of glide symmetries in perpendicular directions using a nearest-neighbor tight-binding model. This model contains horizontal and vertical hopping terms and reveals two distinct non-equivalent Dirac cones within the first Brillouin zone along a high-symmetry path. These cones can be modified through various perturbations of the Hamiltonian. These perturbations disrupt the lattice symmetries by applying differing onsite potentials at the lattice sites, which causes the Dirac cones to collapse into semi-Dirac cones and nodal lines along the high-symmetry paths. Next, we applied a dimerization to the hopping terms and observed the migration of the Dirac cones across the first Brillouin zone along curved trajectories. Additionally, we outline the potential realization of this model using CO atoms on top of a Cu(111) surface.

Quantum states known as single-photon catalyzed coherent states (SPCCSs) can be generated via quantum-optical catalysis using beam splitters or parametric amplifiers. These states occur when a coherent state and a single-photon state interact in two input ports, and a photon is detected in a specific output channel. We examine the success probabilities associated with detecting these states, as they vary depending on the catalytic device used. Notably, our analysis reveals that states produced by beam splitters and parametric amplifiers exhibit the same characteristics when analyzing the distribution of photons. We thoroughly investigate the unique quantum properties of SPCCSs, including sub-Poisson statistics, anti-bunching effects, and quadrature squeezing. We demonstrate that these quantum traits are more prominent when the device used to create the state is a beam splitter. Additionally, we explore how various parameters influence the SPCCS's Fock expansion coefficients, its distribution of photons, and its quantum traits.

In General Relativity using the Newman-Penrose formalism, the use of biquaternions is effectively reduced to working with bivectors. This requirement is consistently met within the Newman-Penrose formalism, as it is established to represent any Minkowski metric in terms of bivectors in a general form. This finding is extended in this study to an extensive generalization of the Minkowski metric tensor expression using the Newman-Penrose formalism, which is expressed in terms of bivectors in both its standard and expanded forms.

A recent framework combining artificial neural networks and mixed integer linear programming for designing chemical compounds has been built upon to create a new method for polymer inference. This new method incorporates a unique way of depicting polymers using monomers, new descriptors that capture their structure, and employs linear regression in the predictive framework. Computational trials have demonstrated that the proposed approach excels in predicting specific chemical properties in polymers, also successfully modeling compounds composed of up to 50 non-hydrogen atoms within a monomeric structure.

This paper presents a unified approach to addressing certain complex optimization challenges. Problems of control, estimation, and system design can be redefined as optimization problems subject to specific constraints. However, given the infinite dimensionality of these issues, it becomes necessary to employ numerical techniques to approximate a solution. We explore specific methods used in simultaneous direct approaches, specifically the transcription process. Our focus is on collocation, residual integration, and Runge-Kutta schemes, highlighting their applications to a case study related to the ventilator shortage during the COVID-19 pandemic. Our study investigated the possibility of ventilating more than one patient on a single ventilator by estimating patient parameters with a limited number of flow rate measurements, modifying air flow resistance, and controlling the ventilator's pressure to ensure desired tidal volumes for both patients.

Identifying tumors in the esophagus from CT scans can be very difficult for humans or computer systems due to low contrast, the varying shape of the esophagus, and the presence of external objects such as feeding tubes. To compensate for the limitations of automatic methods, professional radiologists spend a significant amount of time manually outlining the tumors. To streamline this process, this research explores the use of active contour models for the automatic delineation of tumors in CT scans, focusing on endoscopic and axial views and taking into account tumor characteristics. The proposed method utilizes an active contour model guided by image gradients, with an optimization approach to minimize the influence of external factors and better accommodate the exothermic nature of the gradient field. The study's results show that the proposed model achieves greater accuracy compared to other segmentation techniques, with a minimum total variation error of 6.89 milliliters and a minimum diameter difference error of 2.42 millimeters.

The success of offshore drilling operations relying on subsurface resources heavily depends on geosteering, a real-time field practice for adjusting the wellbore trajectory to stay near a productive reservoir. Adjusting the wellbore path through manual adjustment of the drill bit's orientation and rotational direction is a practice for controlling the wellbore trajectory. However, these adjustments can only be made within a certain angular range due to limited equipment capabilities, which can significantly affect the wellbore's ability to navigate along a desired trajectory. This paper presents a method for estimating the wellbore's spatial position and location relative to a geological formation by fusing measurements from a directional tool and x-ray computed tomography. The approach leverages the equipment's ability to measure the wellbore's orientation in space and uses data from previous drilling operations to model the geological formation, which can be visually visualized to validate the approach. This method utilizes a forward modeling equation to predict the tool's readings based on geological formation models, which are then used to update the model in real-time by minimizing a mathematical function that accounts for measurement noise and model updates. This approach provides a valuable tool for visualizing geological formation models to validate the approach, which can be used to estimate the wellbore's spatial position and relative location to the reservoir.

Named entity recognition (NER) is a fundamental task in natural language processing and a core extraction technique, extensively used to retrieve text-based information for further analysis. One type of NER, nested NER, focuses on recognizing entities within other entities. Most existing nested NER studies apply linear models, which do not adequately capture the hierarchical nature of nested entities. This work overcomes this limitation by modeling nested entities as an integrated whole and proposing a new parsing algorithm to accurately identify all entities at once. Moreover, to address the lack of corpus-level information in NER, this study introduces features based on corpus statistics, including Point-wise Mutual Information, to enhance model performance and adaptability from sentence-level to corpus-level. Our experiments demonstrate that our holistic model, combined with the custom-designed parsing algorithm, significantly improves precision and recall, and that the additional corpus-based features yield substantial performance gains, particularly in low-resource languages.

Research into the location detection of mobile nodes within wireless sensor networks is currently ongoing. We develop and test an innovative RSSI-based location finding method suitable for 802.15.4 (ZigBee) networks. To counteract interference between different technologies operating in the same frequency range, we design and execute a new method for calculating the distance between nodes. The aim of this approach is to minimize the average error in location estimation, and when compared to ideal, interference-free results, we have achieved a level of accuracy of less than half a metre using actual hardware.

Multilingual individuals possess a high level of proficiency in two or more languages, enabling effective written and oral communication across multiple languages. When communicating, they may blend languages, also known as code-switching or code-mixing, by switching between different languages within a single utterance. This research explores current NLP developments, constraints, and potential obstacles in tackling five critical issues affecting multilingual communities: crisis management, healthcare, election campaigns, fake news dissemination, and hate speech. To move forward, we outline potential future datasets, models, and resources to enhance NLP applications for societal betterment, exemplified through an analysis of code-mixing between English and Hindi but with implications for other language combinations.

Human-generated descriptions are commonly used to train and evaluate image description systems, which are typically ranked based on their similarity to these descriptions. This method's reliability hinges on the quality of these descriptions. Since, as demonstrated in Section 2, current datasets are inadequate, I believe we require more precise guidelines balancing visually impaired users' needs and practical description generation feasibility. High-quality reference data could be ideal for system evaluation, yet we should also consider other alternatives.

Tantalum oxide compounds, with the formula Ta$_2$O$_5$, are distinguished by unique properties including high dielectric values and minimal reflectivity. Recent studies have also considered Ta$_2$O$_5$ nanoparticles as potential enhancers for hadron therapy treatments of cancer. To understand the material's electronic behavior, researchers have used theoretical simulations to analyze Ta$_2$O$_5$ in different crystal forms, focusing on how electrons behave in the valence and conduction bands. In addition, researchers have examined the interactions between light and Ta$_2$O$_5$, as well as its interaction with X-rays, to gain a deeper insight into the material's optical properties. Furthermore, simulations have been used to determine the distribution of electrons within Ta$_2$O$_5$, while experimental analysis using a scanning transmission X-ray microscope has verified the material's composition. With this information, researchers have been able to map the distribution of Ta$_2$O$_5$'s electrons, while analyzing how the material responds to the absorption of X-rays, to gain a further insight into the material's behavior under the influence of X-rays.

Previous studies attributed online misinformation dissemination to personal factors, social influences, and search engine recommendations, with seisinism being a relevant personality trait. However, examining how news spreads within a closed environment like university campuses and across different states within the same country is vital, especially considering states' varying characteristics and characteristics similar to personality traits. Unfortunately, there has been limited exploration of this similarity within contextual domains, including online environments. To investigate this, we analyzed the circulation patterns of different types of information (personalized, social influence included) within a network and across time, using a dataset of real and fake news stories that broke in the US during 2016-2020. We discovered that conscientiousness had the most significant effect on constituting a similar profile for states in terms of information spread, with states' scores correlating strongly with their political alignment and voter preferences. Additionally, we found that stories that broke in one state often replicated themselves in other states with similar scores, particularly for information with seisinism-related effects.

We introduce a groundbreaking, efficient, and user-friendly detection algorithm called HALFADO. HALFADO uses a limited number of human judgments to effectively identify anomalies in real-time, high-frequency data streams, such as online advertising clicks. By leveraging a semi-supervised learning approach, we achieve high precision with minimal human input, leveraging a unique confidence calibration method, a targeted data resampling technique, and a self-correction mechanism. Our self-designed evaluation framework rigorously tests the performance of detection algorithms across multiple scenarios, and the results demonstrate HALFADO's superiority over traditional methods in terms of detection accuracy and human resource efficiency.

Humans employ spoken language to efficiently teach other people various skills. Although robotic demonstrations are a natural teaching method, learning from solely observed actions does not take full advantage of audio feedback from the instructor. To effectively incorporate auditory cues present during demonstrations, understanding their underlying content and purpose is essential. This study examines audio input from humans instructing a robot using Sawyer via spoken language by analyzing three key features: speech duration, tone variation, and speech content. Evaluating these features across four dimensions, it was discovered that instructors frequently use the same vocabulary to describe specific task elements despite varying situations such as task types, audio instructions, and errors encountered during demonstrations. However, differences in speech patterns including duration and inflection are present across these conditions, showing that human speech carries significant, potentially valuable information for enhancing robotic learning through demonstration-based methods.

Building on previous work, we propose an algorithm to randomly generate ordered trees of any degree, based on a pre-specified sequence of numbers representing possible node connections. Our method allows for the generation of binary, n-ary trees, or those with various connection patterns. We demonstrate that this algorithm is both accurate and efficient, running in O(n) time with 'n' representing the number of desired nodes. Additionally, we explore potential applications of the algorithm, illustrating its use in deriving formulas by utilizing the underlying proof of correctness.

Quantum field theory complexity is particularly hard to define, especially when transitioning beyond simple free models and their corresponding Gaussian representations. A promising approach to address this difficulty is through the study of conformal field theories in 1+1 dimensions, specifically focusing on the universal sector of the energy-momentum tensor in this context. A key unifying framework consists of Euler-Arnold equations and their broader integro-differential generalizations, ensuring the well-posedness of state or operator complexity optimization problems. Our comprehensive investigation extends upon our prior findings in arXiv:2005.02665, delving into intricate details of employed methodologies. A notable discussion involves differential regularization strategies, solving the integro-differential equation for Fubini-Study state complexity, and further exploring the underlying geometric properties.

Conversational interfaces are becoming ubiquitous, and systems with these interfaces are being widely used in various settings by many individuals. Although they have achieved considerable success, the infrastructure for automated testing of these systems lags behind traditional software systems. To enhance the quality of conversational systems, developers require a robust automated testing framework that streamlines the process of crafting, executing, and updating test cases. This paper outlines our ongoing research in developing an automated testing framework for conversational agents in Python, and highlights the key challenges faced in this endeavor. Specifically, we highlight the difficulties in establishing a precise specification for desired system behavior and comparing the meaning of utterances.

Using a sophisticated mathematical model known as the Fisher information matrix, it's possible to estimate the measurement uncertainties that a hypothetical "Planet X" would contribute, based on existing observations of the solar system's outer planets. Analyzing the solar system's configuration in 2018, we found that measuring "Planet X" within this distance range typically carries an uncertainty of approximately 20 million kilometers (or about 0.3 AU). Specifically, if "Planet X" were located at 400 AU from the sun, our model predicts a median uncertainty of approximately 27 million kilometers (or 0.4 AU). However, there are regions in the solar system where the uncertainty drops below 10 million kilometers (or 0.1 AU), providing the optimal windows to detect "Planet X" with the most accurate results, including an estimated uncertainty of about 0.07 AU, primarily when Mars and the outer planets are aligned in the sky. These findings can be applied to various types of gravitational influences that "Planet X" might have on the solar system's configuration.

Previous studies have demonstrated that Translation Memory (TM) can enhance Neural Machine Translation (NMT) performance. Unlike existing approaches which rely on bilingual corpora for TM and employ source-side similarity searches, our proposed framework leverages monolingual data and retrieves memories in a cross-lingual manner. Notably, our framework offers two significant advantages: firstly, it enables vast amounts of monolingual data to be incorporated into TM; secondly, both the memory retriever and the NMT model can be jointly optimized for translation objectives. Experimental results indicate that the proposed method achieves substantial gains in performance and outperforms TM-augmented NMT baselines even with bilingual TM. Furthermore, our model's capacity to tap into monolingual data allows it to excel in low-resource and domain adaptation scenarios.

Researchers have suggested that specific patterns in the Cosmic Microwave Background, namely low-variance circles and Hawking points, could provide evidence for the Conformal Cyclic Cosmology model. These patterns are predicted to originate from previous black hole mergers and evaporation events. We analyzed the Planck and WMAP data using a machine learning tool called HawkingNet, and initially found potential anomalies resembling low-variance circles and Hawking points. However, these anomalies were later removed, and upon re-examination, we found no statistically significant evidence supporting the existence of low-variance circles or Hawking points. Our analysis does indicate the presence of local non-Gaussian fluctuations in the CMB, suggesting that the real sky may differ from theoretical predictions.

This paper builds upon previous work of the second author with Daskalopoulos and Vazquez, which involved introducing a Yamabe flow based on fractional curvature and demonstrating the existence of mild solutions. The current research expands on that study by establishing the convergence of the flow under certain data conditions within a broader framework. The new results are derived from an approach simplified by Struwe in his book.

To recognize new categories from minimal labeled data, few-shot learning has been rapidly evolving in recent years. However, traditional methods that rely on average features can sometimes utilize noisy information. This research proposes a new network structure called the Attention Meta-Bagging Module, which is designed to build a diverse ensemble of expert models that can filter noise and gain complementary information through the attention mechanism. By incorporating this module into the training process, the model learns multiple specialized branches that are guided by the attention weights, and the subsequent selection of the most suitable branch ensures better generalization ability. The module's ability to focus on key information and filter noise is supported by the information theory, which guides the maximization and minimization of mutual information between tasks and the bag with high and low correlation tasks, respectively. This research shows that the proposed module's effectiveness is supported by experiments on the Mini-ImageNet and Meta-FewShot-NCIFW datasets, which demonstrate superior performance and are supported by visual ablation studies.

Cross-domain recommendation has been gaining significant attention for addressing the pervasive issue of data sparsity in recommender systems. Single-domain recommendation models are commonly employed, but they are limited by the additional requirement of identifying usable sparse items. In this work, we introduce an innovative approach that leverages multiple sparse domains to enhance performance in a primary target domain through two novel strategies. Firstly, we propose a Multi-Sparse-Domain Attention Network (MSDAN) which utilizes attention mechanisms to capture the importance of varying sparse domains. By allocating different weights to different domains, the model can capture the characteristics of different user preferences in each domain. Secondly, we introduce a Target-Domain Connection Network (TDCN) to counterbalance the utilization of different domains by learning how to connect target and sparse domains. By learning how to transfer knowledge from different domains to the target domain, the model can differentiate between domains and different user preferences. The proposed models are part of a comprehensive framework called Multi-Sparse-Domain Collaborative Recommendation (MSDCR) which achieves enhanced performance in cross-domain recommendation. Our model is evaluated on eight real-world datasets and its efficacy is validated through superior performance compared to state-of-the-art single and cross-domain recommendation models.

Convex optimization issues often take on a more manageable form when represented with conic formulations that leverage a wide variety of exotic cones. Exotic cones in this context, refer to specialized geometric shapes with properties enabling efficient implementation of computational tools, specifically barrier oracles for their own and dual shapes. This work introduces Hypatia, an interior-point solver designed to handle these complex shapes with ease. Developed using Julia and interfacing with JuMP, Hypatia can utilize a wide assortment of predefined exotic cones. It then generates simplified equivalent formulations for various optimization applications that can provide significant improvements in processing speed and memory consumption. The proposed method demonstrates a marked improvement in problem-solving efficiency when compared to more conventional and complex conic formulations.

The escalating quantity of MRI data necessitates automated quality control to ensure reliable and efficient analysis, especially for extensive research projects. Several approaches have been explored to develop scalable and dependable quality control pipelines, but effectively generalizing these methods across diverse, previously unseen data remains a significant challenge. In this study, we focused on identifying key elements that enable MRI quality control pipelines to perform optimally, with an eye on creating a universal framework. We utilized diverse datasets to test various components, including anomaly detection and image regression models, and found that a combination of the VAE and CNN architectures yielded the best results. As part of our research, we assembled and utilized the EZI benchmark, consisting of 2350 healthy and pathological MRI images across multiple pathologies and protocols, to evaluate the generalization capabilities of quality control pipelines. We demonstrated that a refined version of our proposed pipeline, labeled Universal EZI (UEZI), outperformed several alternative methods on external data in EZI analysis, with plans to release the UEZI framework for public use.

To understand how private electric vehicles influence the recovery of power grids following outages, we developed a mathematical framework that incorporates decentralized decision-making in both transportation and energy systems. We utilized multi-agent optimization to model this process and overcame computational challenges through an efficient algorithm based on precise reformation. Numerical analysis was conducted to demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach, yielding valuable policy insights and paving the way for further study into grid resilience with private EVs within interconnected transportation and energy networks.

Intel's Optane DC Persistent Memory Module (DC PMM) has reached commercial viability as the first commercially available nonvolatile memory DIMM. It offers fast, byte-granular data access similar to DRAM, combined with power-fail safe storage. In-depth performance evaluations have shown Optane DC PMMs to excel as primary memory, eliminating the need for secondary storage and enabling new algorithms that combine the capabilities of primary memory and CPU cache. Existing performance studies have showcased the potential of Optane DC PMMs and validated their performance benefits, however optimal configurations and memory management configurations for specific workloads and application types have yet to be determined. In this study, various configurations and memory management strategies are systematically evaluated through extensive benchmark tests on a multi-core system equipped with Intel Xeon E5-2699 v3 CPUs and Optane DC PMMs, focusing on persistent memory management. Nine different management policies were assessed, as well as non-managed and primary RAM scenarios, on the persistent system. Our research demonstrates that the best performance is highly workload-dependent, stressing the complexity of developing universal optimization guidelines. In particular, we found that the default persistent memory management provided by the optane file system yielded suboptimal performance in many cases. New management approaches, such as the optane-raw policy, consistently outperformed the existing default management, achieving up to 2.5x better performance in certain tests. Our research further highlights the need for default CPU cache utilization on Optane DC

The Motivation Dynamics framework, a concept explored in recent studies that applies bifurcations to model an autonomous agent's decision-making processes, is further developed to accommodate multiple autonomous entities in this paper. We demonstrate how the framework's capabilities can be expanded to capture persistent, cooperative behavior between agents meeting at specific locations, and through in-depth analysis and numerical data, reveal that this extension exhibits a complex pattern indicative of a strange attractor.

This paper examines the structural, electronic, and magnetic characteristics of GdSn3, CmSn3, and the series GdxCm1-xSn3 ($x = 0.25$, $0.5$, and $0.75$) using a full-potential linearized augmented plane wave method within the generalized gradient approximation+U. We studied the fundamental properties of bulk GdSn3, CmSn3, and GdxCm1-xSn3 materials crystallizing in the AuCu3 structure. Our results match previous experimental and theoretical data on the GdSn3 compound and indicate that CmSn3 and GdSn3 both adopt a type-A anti-ferromagnetic configuration and display metallic behavior. Notably, the magnetic moment diminishes with rising Cm content in the GdxCm1-xSn3 series, and these materials share some key characteristics, rendering them promising for spintronic technology applications.

The paper reviews predictions made by an extension of the standard model called the bilepton model, which involves changing the fundamental symmetry group from $SU(2) \times U(1)$ to $SU(3)\times U(1)$, while assigning the three fermion families in a non-consecutive manner. For consistency, three fermion families are necessary as indicated by triangle anomaly cancellation and asymptotic freedom. In the bilepton model, novel physical phenomena are predicted to occur, including bileptons and three types of heavy quarks: ${\cal D}$, ${\cal S}$, and ${\cal T}$. Theoretical calculations suggest that Quantum Chromodynamics will result in heavy quarks bonding to each other or light quarks to form composite particles like baryons and mesons that might be detectable with a next-generation 100 TeV particle accelerator but are too heavy for the current LHC.

A group of transformations $G$ for a graph $\mathcal X$ is termed as an 'ox' (or precise ox if uniquely so) when every element within $G$ can be expressed as a shortest-word using the generating set $D$. This concept has been extensively studied for non-abelian groups since its introduction in~\cite{Chen2019}, with recent applications in~\cite{ogssch,ogsglpn,ogsglnx,ogsglx}. However, a comprehensive analysis linking the ox property to geometric characteristics of the graph $\mathcal X$ or its geometric properties is still lacking. In this paper, we establish a connection between the ox property and the geometry of the graph $\mathcal X$ through a new geometric parameter $\omega_G\geqslant 1$. This parameter signifies that specific subgroups of $G$ with isomorphic representation to $D$ and $D^{-1}$ are either single or come in pairs. Moreover, $G$ possesses the ox property precisely when $\omega_G=1$. As an illustration, we demonstrate that $G=\operatorname{GL}(2,\mathbb Z[n])$ is ox with respect to its canonical generating set for any integer $n\geqslant 3$.

Typically, the impact of dark matter halos on supernovae observations through weak lensing is considered as a means of measuring the curvature of the universe through a large-scale effect, excluding the local influence. In our research, we challenge this assumption by demonstrating that the local dark matter lensing effect cannot be disregarded and must be accounted for when interpreting supernovae data in the context of the expanding universe or dark energy. To counter the assumption of isotropic lensing, we developed a method to incorporate the direction-dependent distortion caused by matter distributions into our calculations. By integrating this model with the HubbleFlow supernovae catalog and assuming a Planck 2018 cosmological model, we discovered an average deviation of -0.049 in supernovae magnitudes, amounting to approximately 5% of the total lensing effect and 15% of the total variance in the data, which has a comparable effect to the total uncertainty in the equation of state parameter in the $\Lambda$CDM model. Our findings suggest that including this directional variable could provide a new, independent approach to measuring the intrinsic variance in the Hubble constant and the expansion history of the universe.

These are lecture notes for a 6-hour mini-course on stochastic partial differential equations presented at the University of Oxford in April-May 2021. 
The main objective of these lecture notes is to provide an in-depth explanation of the variational method for monotone and coercive stochastic partial differential equations. 
They also briefly cover the use of mild solutions for semi-linear parabolic equations with smooth and bounded diffusion coefficients, as well as an overview of the connection between the variational and non-degenerate approaches.

The development of efficient and controllable quantum communication networks will depend heavily on reliable creation and manipulation of solid-state devices that interface photons with electronic spins effectively. In silicon material, T-type damage centers have shown significant potential for this interface, thanks to their unique optical properties in the O-band region and long-lived electronic and nuclear spin lifetimes. Although research on these defect centers has so far been conducted as part of bulk silicon studies, we demonstrate the consistent creation of high T center densities within the 220nm device layer of Silicon-On-Insulator (SOI) wafers, using a process that combines ion implantation and heat treatment. By developing a method to measure spin-dependent optical transitions, we found that high T center densities located near the interface can exhibit similar characteristics to bulk T centers, indicating a new pathway for exploring and integrating T center-based quantum technologies in SOI photonics.

MRI technology utilizes radio waves to scan the human body and obtain precise, pain-free diagnostic images. These images enable radiologists to visually assess anatomy and physiological processes within the body, ultimately facilitating early disease diagnosis and treatment. Advanced imaging capabilities, combined with sophisticated processing techniques, enable detection of hard-to-spot tumors. This assignment delves into Automated Tumor Detection by comparing conventional image processing methods, such as morphological analysis and regional growth algorithms, in order to explore their application and effectiveness.

In this research, we explore the properties of a novel algebraic variant of the degenerate Bernoulli polynomial $\tilde{\beta}_{k}(m,x)$, as well as its corresponding degenerate Bernoulli number. This investigation is grounded in an algebraic framework that builds upon the foundational work of Cha and Kim regarding orthogonal and biorthogonal functions, as presented in their respective papers on Hopf algebras and combinatorial applications, as well as on their more recent contribution in the realm of combinatorial mathematics and algebraic number theory.

The high activity levels of M dwarfs present a significant challenge for discovering exoplanets, as their stellar activity masks the signals from exoplanets. This problem requires an in-depth understanding of the various planetary and stellar indicators it impacts. To address this problem, researchers are developing tools to detect extrinsic variations in the stars' activity cycles. In this study, we focus on the M dwarf GJ 1146 and conduct an extensive analysis of its activity, including observations of its magnetic field direction, radial velocity, and transit timing variations. We also compare its activity levels to those of M dwarfs with known exoplanets, noting that while its activity appears moderate, there are signs of rapid fluctuations. These observations suggest that similar studies on active phases of M dwarfs are essential for confirming the existence of exoplanets, particularly when verifying the mass of low-mass planets with precise measurements. Ultimately, this research emphasizes the importance of considering stellar activity when interpreting the observations of M dwarfs and the need for further study of their active phases.

This research paper proposes a pair of methods for designing a flexible and efficient data collection process in Wireless Sensor Networks, ensuring high reliability and performance. Firstly, a link quality estimation technique is utilized, enabling swift computation of link quality between nodes. Secondly, a hierarchical sector-based system is established to organize and coordinate nodes within each sector to minimize interference and improve data transmission. The effectiveness of these methods was demonstrated through a protocol, called HBCP, developed and evaluated in a simulated environment utilizing TinyOS and TelosB devices. The outcome of the evaluation revealed that HBCP can achieve very high reliability levels, particularly in large-scale networks and networks prone to bottlenecks.

The use of context in deep learning-based object detectors has the potential to improve their ability to recognize objects. However, there is a lack of consistent evaluation methods for assessing context usage. In this work, we categorize object detectors that use context into three groups: those that do not utilize context, those that use implicit context, and those that explicitly utilize context. We provide a detailed analysis of the mechanisms by which context is used in the evaluation of three context networks we have proposed in the companion paper (https://arxiv.org/abs/2111.09584). In addition, we present a comprehensive dataset consisting of 30 object detectors that use context, along with their publicly available implementations. We have also established a unified framework for evaluating these detectors, which can be adapted to other context-using detectors. The evaluation results demonstrate that context-using detectors generally perform better than those that do not use context, but there is room for improvement, particularly with the implicit context detectors. The code, models, and datasets we have provided are available for free use, along with the code for evaluating other context-using detectors.

The main objective of this paper is to investigate multiple solution possibilities for a specific Kirchhoff type elliptic system of equations that are given by the system of equations where $m\left(\sum^k_{j=1}\|u_j\|^2\right)\Delta u_i=\frac{f_i(x,u_1,\ldots,u_k)}{|x|^\beta}+\varepsilon h_i(x)$ holds for $i=1,\ldots,k$, within the bounded domain $\Omega$ in $\mathbb{R}^2$, where $x$ contains the origin with smooth boundary, and for a certain condition $\beta\in [0,2)$; here $m$ denotes a function that belongs to Kirchhoff type, $f_i$ behave like $e^{\beta s^2}$, and there is a function $h_i\in \left(\big(H^1_0(\Omega)\big)^*,\|\cdot\|_*\right)$. By making use of a singular Trudinger-Moser inequality for a small positive value $\varepsilon$ and variational methods, we are able to establish sufficient conditions for a multiplicity of the system's solutions given the given conditions.

We examine the concentration behavior of functionals of random vectors whose entries reside in the discrete cube. These vectors must adhere to either the stochastic covering property (SCP) or the strong Rayleigh property (SRP). Our findings regarding SCP measures yield new subgaussian inequalities of a bounded-difference type, surpassing earlier results by Pemantle and Peres (2015). Specifically, our work provides an $n^{1/4}$ improvement in the initial term of these inequalities, matching the outcome from Pemantle and Peres' weakly log-concave inequality of a bounded-difference type. Moreover, building on SRP measures, we establish a novel inequality of a variancesum-of-products type for the determinant of a projection matrix formed from an anti-symmetric Bernoulli matrix with entries drawn from the anti-platonic distribution. This result extends results from Bunyakovsky (1999) and Tao and Vu (2002), offering an explicit constant in the inequality's formulation. Notably, our constant outperforms previous outcomes by a factor of $\pi^2/8 \approx 0.39$ smaller, addressing an earlier conjecture regarding the asymptotic behavior of these inequalities as described in Bunyakovsky (2015). Additionally, our work involves a general lower bound estimate for functions of SCP or SRP functions of matrix-valued random vectors. This bound, depending on the matrix dimensions, serves a specific type

Let $k$ be a perfect field of characteristic greater than two, and consider the ring of power series $R$ over the Witt vectors of $k$, expanded in variables $t_1, \dots, t_d$. The main aim of this study is to generalize classical Fontaine-Messing theory to a base ring of the form $R$. Notably, we establish theorems enabling the comparison of crystalline and \'etale cohomologies with torsion coefficients for smooth schemes $X$ over $R$.

This study explores the double longitudinal-spin asymmetry in semi-inclusive deep inelastic scattering where hadron pairs' transverse momentum is not considered. Specifically, we investigate the cause of the cosine azimuthal asymmetry in hadron production, accounting for the connection between the helicity distribution $g_1$ and the twist-3 dihadron fragmentation function. Using a spectator model, we calculate the interference term between $s$-wave and $p$-wave and estimate this asymmetry at various experiments, including COMPASS, JLab 12 GeV, and the future EIC. Our analysis suggests that the cosine azimuthal asymmetry in SIDIS can serve as a key test for the dihadron fragmentation function.

We've established recently, much like our work on Deformed Special Relativity, that Fock's coordinate transformation can be developed from a novel, deformed form of the Poisson brackets.  Utilizing this approach, we successfully obtained the associated momentum transformation, which preserves the four-dimensional relationship between momentum and space, p_{\mu} x^{\mu}.  With the deformed algebra in hand, we derive the first Casimir invariant in this paper.  Following first quantization, we utilize the Klein-Gordon equation to show that Fock's spacetime corresponds to the de Sitter universe, whose spacetime radius can be defined by the invariant length representing the de Sitter hypersurface.

Wilberd van der Kallen translated this 1951 thesis into English, originally written by T.A. Springer. Springer investigated the method of categorizing conjugacy classes within the symplectic group Sp_n(K), specifically focusing on fields K with a characteristic other than two. His work revealed that each conjugacy class can be distinguished using a combination of invariant characteristics. These characteristics initially mirror those found in the general linear group – namely, irreducible polynomials and systems of non-negative integers – but also incorporate additional properties, such as unique configurations of Hermitian forms and quadratic forms, each belonging to a specific equivalence class.

This paper presents a Wikipedia-based entity recommendation framework that utilizes an embedding approach, where the Wikipedia database is hierarchically divided into layered graphs to extract entity features and learn entity representations. By combining the extracted information with an advanced ranking method, this framework recommends related entities to those in the Wikipedia. Experimental evaluations with diverse datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach, yielding superior performance compared to other embedding and traditional ranking methods. Furthermore, a case study visually displays entity features and the Wikipedia graph structure to illustrate the approach's efficacy.
